earlier_scan.source_named: Jamil, Hussain & John Newman. 1987. Limbang Bisaya: Society and Language. Sarawak Museum Journal 36(58), 75-89 (named in Wikipedia refs; not online); Glottolog entry retired into Brunei Bisaya

sources.citation: Nothofer, Bernd. 1991. The languages of Brunei Darussalam. In H. Steinhauer (ed.), Papers in Austronesian Linguistics No. 1, 151-176. Pacific Linguistics A-81.
sources.note: Dusun/Bisaya (Bebuloh informant) treated as mutually intelligible dialects; only phonetic remark is r ~ gh; Swadesh lists unmarked for stress. No stress hits on re-a full-text search for stress/accent.
Retired entry: 'Merged into Bisaya, Brunei [bsb]' per change request 2007-206; no descriptive references listed.

sources.citation: [IJRISS authors] 2025. Navigating the Currents: The Language Ecology of Limbang Bisaya. International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science 9(11): 4874-4879.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic (language ecology); no phonology; states 'studies on the Bisaya language are very limited'. Reference list names Chong 2025, Yabit Alas 2019, Md. Roslan 2020 (all sociolinguistic). Silent.

sources.citation: Gardiner, Ishamina Athirah, David Deterding & Yabit Alas. 2019. The pronunciation of Dusun. Southeast Asia: A Multidisciplinary Journal 19: 14-21 (Brunei Dusun, Tutong district; same ISO code bsb).
sources.note: Consonants, vowels, syllable structure, NWS passage; re-a full-text search for stress/accent: no 'stress', 'accent', 'tekanan'. Silent (and describes Brunei Dusun, not the Limbang variety).

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2016. North Borneo Sourcebook: Vocabularies and Functors. PALI Language Texts: Southeast Asia. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press (author's print-ready PDF on R. David Zorc's site).
sources.note: Sec. 3 'Limbang Bisaya (LBISAYA, Bisaya-Lotud subgroup)' p. 23 gives elicitation sites (Lembuak, Pangkalan Jawa, Pengkalan Madang, Tedungon, Batu Danau, Bidang, Tanjong in Limbang district 2009-2013; Bebuloh, Brunei 2010), pronouns, demonstratives; wordlists pp. 69-272 carry no stress marks; 'stress', 'accent', 'prosody' occur nowhere in the book. Silent.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. hdl:10125/101972.
sources.note: Limbang Bisaya appears only in 4.3.5 (pronoun replacement) and 11.4.6 (pp. 398-399, subgrouping/history). The only stress discussion is Philippine (8.2.9 Contrastive accent; fn. 3 p. 287: 'most languages native to Mindanao and areas further south have lost contrastive stress'). No Limbang Bisaya stress statement.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-206 (Dave Moody, SIL-MLB): merge [bsd] Bisaya, Sarawak and [ttx] Tutong 1 into [bsb] Bisaya, Brunei; adopted 2008-01-14.
sources.note: Nothing; identity record only: 'Bisaya in Brunei and Sarawak is the same cross-border language.. Brunei Bisaya, which includes as dialects Sarawak Bisaya and Tutong 1/Southern Bisaya' (pp. 2-3).

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 1971 (deposited 2014). Field notebook RB2-003-A, Sarawak; notebook pp. 31-40 'Bisaya (Limbang dialect)', speaker Sylvester Sarnagi of Ukong, Oct. 1971. Kaipuleohone, University of Hawai'i Digital Language Archive, hdl:10125/33159.
sources.note: Unpublished primary data, no prose statement. page scan (notebook pp. 32-33) verified by this reader: every stress tick on a polysyllable precedes the FINAL syllable (a'buk 'hair; dust', ka'bay, bi'biy 'lips', i'pən, di'lə?, ta'li, mi'kit, ma'to, ku'ku?, ka'kət, jəla'mə?, mi'nit, mu'yu?, a'su, məma'nuk, a'lad, i'ku?, la'nut, un'tu, təmu'lud, bəna'tay, ma'tay, bəsin'də?, nu'təb, na'gəd); no penult ticks. Implicit evidence of final-syllable prominence in citation forms only.
Vowel and consonant tables (sourced to Yabit Alas 1994 and Jamil & Newman 1987); no stress statement. Only three references.

sources.citation: Kroeger, Paul R. [pre-publication draft]. Language classification in Sarawak: a status report. Sarawak Museum Journal.
sources.note: Bisaya only in classification (Dusun-Bisaya group; notes Blust's wordlists for Bisaya Bukit and Limbang Bisaya). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Hussain bin Jamil & John Newman. 1987. Limbang Bisaya: society and language. Sarawak Museum Journal 37 (n.s. 58): 75-89 (language section, pp. c. 77-89). Malay version: Dewan Bahasa 31(5): 374-388.

sources.note: The only published description of Limbang (Sarawak) Bisaya specifically; its language section compares LB phonology with Asmah 1983's Beaufort Bisaya and is the most likely place for a stress statement. Only pp. 75-76 are free online.
